title: Elastic Slices PRD — fractional reserved leases, soft-burst orchestration, and isolation contracts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers want lower-cost reserved capacity with predictable baseline throughput but also safe, short bursts when traffic spikes. Current reserved pools are coarse (full-slot reservations) and either overprovision or cause hard throttles.

Goal: Deliver an "elastic slices" feature for Dedicated that lets tenants lease fractional GPU capacity as time-bound slices (e.g., 25% for 4h), with an orchestrated soft-burst path to absorb transient spikes without breaking isolation guarantees. The product combines: (1) reservation API for creating/renewing fractional leases, (2) scheduler changes to admit slices + best-effort transient burst capacity, (3) isolation contracts that define preemption/quota-decay behavior, and (4) billing/telemetry changes to surface unit economics per-slice.

Scope (MVP):
- Reservation API endpoints: CreateSlice, RenewSlice, ReleaseSlice, QuerySliceStatus.
- Slice admission in allocator: represent slices as weighted capacity tokens; admit fractional allocations on nodes with slack.
- Soft-burst orchestration: short-lived best-effort buffer pool (ephemeral capacity) that can be borrowed when slices hit short spikes; automatic fallback to hosted models or lower-quantized variants when borrowed capacity is exhausted.
- Isolation contract: tenant-configurable policy enum {strict, graceful, tolerant} that controls preemption order and token decay.
- Observability: per-slice telemetry (utilization, burst borrow events, preemption events) and cost breakdown on Console.

Out of scope for MVP: multi-region lease negotiation, cross-tenant credit markets, UI for self-serve slice tuning (console surfaces only basic metrics in MVP).
acceptance_criteria: API: CreateSlice accepted and returns lease id with capacity fraction and TTL; unit tests cover invalid fractions and TTL validation.

Scheduler: allocator can pack fractional slices onto nodes and report per-node reserved fraction; integration test demonstrates 10 tenants at varying fractions occupying a single node without violating max_utilization <= 100%.

Soft-burst: when a tenant's QPS increases 3x for <=60s, requests may be served from ephemeral buffer pool without increasing tail latency above 2x baseline 95th P50 < 200ms for generator models and < 300ms for chat models during borrow events.
Isolation contracts: preemption behavior for 'graceful' policy reduces slice capacity by 25% first, then 50%, then full reclaim; verified via automated chaos test injected preemption signals.
Fallbacks: if ephemeral pool exhausted, route new requests to allowed fallback model variants defined on tenant config and surface routed-fallback metrics in Console within 10 minutes of rollout.
Billing: slices are billed prorated by lease duration and fraction; billing test vectors align with finance spreadsheet and show expected invoice line items for 0.25 fractional slice for 4 hours.
Observability: Console shows per-slice utilization, burst events, and preemption counts for last 7d; dashboards load under 2s for up to 1k slices in a tenant's view.
Security: API honors existing RBAC—only tenant admins or service accounts with reserved:write may create/renew slices.
engineering_notes: Allocator representation: represent slices as (node_capacity * fraction) and track residual capacity as floating point; to reduce scheduling churn we will quantize fractions to multiples of 0.05 for MVP.
Trade-offs: quantization reduces packing efficiency but simplifies preemption accounting and billing accuracy.
Kernel/runtime impact: ephemeral borrow pool will be backed by opportunistic preemptible instances — requires ENG-48211 support for preemptible eviction hooks and KV cache draining within 5s.
Compatibility: must maintain existing P99 latency SLOs for Dedicated tenants with 'strict' isolation; scheduling heuristics will prioritize strict-policy tenants when packing nodes.
Backwards compatibility: tenants without slice leases should be unaffected; API returns 404 for non-dedicated projects.
rollout_plan: Week 1: API and schema landed behind feature flag; internal e2e tests and contract tests added.
Week 2: Allocator changes merged in canary pool; run cluster-level chaos tests (preemption, node drain) against canary tenants.
Week 3: Soft-burst ephemeral pool enabled for 10 pilot customers via opt-in; collect telemetry for 72 hours and run postmortem.
Week 4: Billing connector and Console panels enabled; invite 50% of pilot pool to expand usage.
Gradual 6-week ramp to GA with support runbook and runbook playbooks for oncall.
metrics: Slice adoption: number of active slices and aggregate fraction reserved per-cluster (target 100 slices first month).
Burst borrow rate: percentage of requests served from ephemeral pool when slice utilization > 90%.
Preemption events: count per-tenant per-day and mean time to recovery (target < 120s).
Tail latency during borrow events: 95th and 99th p99 comparison against baseline (target <2x baseline p95).
Billing correlation: invoice line item reconciliation rate (target 100% matching finance spreadsheet for sample tenants).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: packing inefficiency leads to wasted capacity and increased cost — mitigation: quantize fractions, monitor fragmentation metric, and open automatic compaction job if fragmentation > 20%.
Risk: ephemeral borrow pool causes noisy neighbor latency spikes — mitigation: borrow pool capped per-node and per-tenant, and borrow throttles if node latency or GPU utilization exceeds thresholds.
Risk: billing edge cases during renewals/early release — mitigation: implement conservative prorate logic and run reconciliation test vectors with finance prior to GA.
Risk: customer confusion around policies — mitigation: add clear Console descriptions and provide example scenarios in docs and support playbook.
